preview_en:
After securing their greatest footballing achievement in the last UEFA Nations League (UNL) campaign, San Marino make their League C debut against a Finland side who suffered relegation last time around.

Match News and Current Form

San Marino stunned many by registering their first pair of competitive victories on the way to sealing promotion from League D in the previous UNL campaign. Now with the added security of no third-tier relegation due to the tournament’s impending restructure, FIFA’s lowest-ranked nation face a mammoth task to end what is now a 14-game winless run since their promotion-sealing win over Liechtenstein (D1, L13). With a team largely composed of amateur and semi-professional talent, the best San Marino can realistically hope for from these games is to avoid a slew of huge scorelines given they share a group with three top-100 ranked nations.

After competing in the third tier in the inaugural UNL edition, Finland finally returned to League C after three League B campaigns with a dreadful return of six defeats from as many games in the 2024/25 campaign. Finland have had a great deal of soul searching to do after subsequently failing to qualify for the World Cup finals, with their appearance at the delayed Euro 2020 remaining their only major tournament appearance to date. Earning promotion is a realistic ambition for Jacob Friis’ men given that they’re the second-highest ranked side in the group, but having lost to a Malta side ranked outside of FIFA’s top 150 as recently as November 2025, they can’t take anything for granted here.

Head-to-Head History

Finland boast a rather unsurprising perfect winning record across six prior H2Hs, although their last two visits to San Marino saw them triumph by just a single-goal margin.

Hot Stats and Streaks

San Marino got on the scoresheet in each of their last four defeats.

San Marino averaged 4.5 yellow cards per match in the last UNL cycle (18 in four).

Eight of Finland’s last nine internationals saw goals scored in both halves.

Finland have won just one of their last eight internationals on foreign soil (D2, L5).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Nicola Nanni has scored in his last two UNL appearances for San Marino, leaving him just three goals shy of equalling the all-time scoring record after netting in their most recent friendly. Joel Pohjanpalo has enjoyed a strong start to the season with six goal contributions in seven games for Palermo (G4, A2), but he has never scored against San Marino despite featuring in two H2Hs which saw Finland net eight goals!

San Marino’s squad selection hasn’t thrown up any surprises. The exclusion of 2025 Finnish player of the year, Oliver Antman , is the visitors’ most notable absentee.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

San Marino have had no issues scoring of late, so a Finland to win and both teams to score selection could be the best route to take.

Author: Matthew Billon
